review_type: independent structural image review before registration

findings.evidence: Cardinal v2 master retains round lower bowl, long narrow neck, flared mouth and right lunar-arc loop. No copied beer label, cap, amber body or detached top glint is visible.

Compared with v1 master, v2 visibly rounds the bowl, shoulder and flared mouth. Oblique diagnostic shows an open hollow mouth with visible inner wall; cardinal master has a joined rim highlight, not a floating object.

In stage-02-model-3d.png the lower handle terminates as a visibly exposed flat-ended tube over the right shoulder surface. A small light cap/end face is visible at its left tip rather than a continuous blended root. The upper handle also meets the neck with an abrupt cut-looking end. Cardinal master masks this problem by silhouette overlap, so cardinal appearance alone does not establish connected 3D roots.
findings.required_resolution: Inspect actual handle/body intersection and extend or join the lower root into the vessel wall so no exposed terminal cap remains in the diagnostic; verify both roots.

findings.evidence: Hollow opening is explicit in oblique diagnostic but appears as a narrow horizontal highlight in the fixed cardinal master. This is compatible with the level cardinal camera and is not by itself evidence of a sealed cap.

conclusion: Source identity and rounding are supported. Hold unconditional structural acceptance of the 3D model until the exposed lower handle end is resolved or geometry inspection demonstrates a continuous root. Fixed cardinal master reads connected, but oblique diagnostic reveals the endpoint concern.
limits: Image review only: no Blender mesh/topology inspection, generation, game activation or native acceptance.
Model-controls reports reuse of saved v1 Blender geometry, authored wall rounding and no new ImageGen call; this review does not independently audit process execution.
Depth, wall thickness and opaque stylized glass are authored interpretations.
Native liquid, manual seal, liquid-dependent detail and Transparent behavior remain unvalidated and unchanged.
Oblique image is a structural diagnostic, not an additional native orientation or replacement for the fixed cardinal master.
